answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity graph. Before an agent may claim its nectar of rewards, it must lock a stake, and peers attest to one another so a fake identity cannot simply appear. New claims are checked against a mirror of known attestations; agents that wander between aliases without a trusted sponsor are ignored. To mount a Sybil attack, an adversary must fund and link a fresh bond for every false persona, and each detected duplicate forfeits its stake. The cost scales with the number of identities, turning a cheap flood into an expensive bet.
